title: Scheduled Tenant Quiesce and Safe Failback Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the standardized process for scheduling a tenant quiesce (graceful traffic drain and checkpoint), performing maintenance that requires a drained tenant, and executing a verified safe failback. It is intended for Customer Success, Support, and Oncall SREs for Redwood Dedicated and Private tenants. The goal is to minimize customer impact, preserve KV cache and state where applicable, and ensure deterministic rollback/failback criteria.

Scope and use-cases:
- Planned maintenance that requires temporary cessation of writes or reduced throughput for a single tenant (software patches, DB schema migration, KV-store compaction, model swap tests).
- Emergency scheduled windows where a controlled quiesce prevents cascading errors during cross-tenant maintenance.
- NOT for system-wide outages or unscheduled incident evacuations (use incident response runbooks instead).

Preconditions (must be validated before scheduling):
1) Customer agreement: Signed maintenance window or written consent for the proposed time and impact window.
2) Configuration snapshot: Export of tenant config, routing rules, and active model pins (S3 location or config repo tag).
3) Telemetry baseline: Last 7 days of p50/p95 latency, error rate, and token-per-request volume captured and attached to the maintenance ticket.
4) Backup & checkpoint: For tenants with persistent KV cache or embeddings, snapshot/export completed and verified.
5) Runbook ownership: Named oncall/CS lead, SRE lead, and PM on the ticket.
6) Rollback plan documented in the ticket with acceptance criteria and expected timelines.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Customer Success (CS) Owner: primary customer comms, stakeholder scheduling, acceptance of post-maintenance health check.
- SRE Ops Lead: executes quiesce, coordinates with infra owners, validates telemetry and rollback triggers.
- Platform Engineer: runs the maintenance tasks that required quiesce (e.g., DB migration, model rollout).
- Oncall Support: monitors alerts during and after the window and executes the rollback if triggers fire.
- Security/Compliance Rep (if required): validates any data-handling steps.

Maintenance timeline (recommended):
- T-72h: Initial customer notice and proposed window. Attach baseline telemetry and expected impact.
- T-48h: Confirmation of snapshot/backups and ownership. Run preflight checklist (see below).
- T-24h: Final reminder; post runbook link and emergency contact list.
- T-01h: Pre-quiesce verification and dry-run of quiesce checklist without affecting traffic.
- T+0 Start: Execute quiesce, run maintenance, verify, failback, and run post-maintenance checks.
- T+2h (or agreed SLA): Initial customer report and preliminary metrics.
- T+24h: Full post-mortem and metrics delivery.

Pre-quiesce checklist (step-by-step):
1) Verify maintenance ticket and customer consent are present. Record ticket ID in all logs.
2) Notify internal stakeholders in #cs-maintenance Slack channel with tags for oncall and SRE. Use the template below.
3) Ensure canary route exists for a small percentage of traffic to detect regressions during failback (if applicable).
4) Validate backups: confirm checksum of exported KV or embeddings snapshot.
5) Confirm autoscaling and burst configuration is disabled for the tenant to avoid unexpected capacity shifts.
6) Prepare telemetry queries and dashboards: p50/p95 latency, 5xx error rate, token rate, streaming connection drop rate.
7) Validate health check endpoints respond with 200 for control test accounts.

Quiesce procedure (commands and sequence):
1) Mark tenant as maintenance-mode in routing service:
   - CLI: rdctl tenant update --id <TENANT_ID> --maintenance true --reason "scheduled-quiesce-<YYYYMMDD>"
   - This flips routing to drain new requests and directs write-requests to reject with 409 + JSON body {\"code\":\"MAINTENANCE\", \"retry_after_s\":3600}.
2) Wait for active request count to reach threshold (<= 5 active long-poll streams) or max drain timeout (default 600s). Monitor: tenants.active_requests{tenant_id:<TENANT_ID>}.
3) Snapshot live KV cache (if not part of nightly backup):
   - script: s3://redwood-backups/exports/<TENANT_ID>/prequiesce-<ts>.tar.gz
   - verify checksum and file size in the ticket.
4) Disable scheduled background jobs (embedding reindexers, background evals) for tenant via jobs-api.
5) Confirm no writes are accepted by running synthetic write test expecting 409 maintenance response.

Maintenance execution notes:
- Platform Engineers perform the maintenance steps using the maintenance ticket as the source of truth. All changes must be versioned and revertable.
- If the maintenance involves a model swap, keep previous model artifact readily available and do a canary rollback plan.
- For DB migrations, use transactional migration patterns with feature flags where possible; avoid long blocking locks.

Verification (post-maintenance before failback):
1) Run integration smoke tests against a preserved control tenant account. Success = 100% pass for control flows.
2) Confirm telemetry: no new 5xx spikes in the last 5 minutes across system services.
3) Validate model artifacts and checksums match expected values.
4) Run load test at 5% of normal production throughput against canary route. Observe p95 latency and error budget.

Safe failback procedure (step-by-step):
1) Re-enable background jobs and confirm they start without errors. Monitor job failure queues for 5m.
2) Flip routing back from maintenance-mode: rdctl tenant update --id <TENANT_ID> --maintenance false
3) Gradual traffic ramp: increase traffic in steps (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> full) with 5-minute observation windows.
4) During each ramp step validate: p95 latency within 20% of baseline, error rate <= baseline + 0.5%, and no unhandled 500 errors.
5) If any metric breaches the thresholds, immediately revert to previous traffic step and run rollback checklist.

Rollback criteria and actions:
- Trigger rollback if any of the following occur: sustained p95 > baseline + 40% for 3 consecutive observation windows, error rate > baseline + 2% sustained, or any critical functional test fails.
- Rollback steps:
  a) Revert code or model artifact using recorded artifact tag.
  b) Restore tenant snapshot from pre-quiesce backup if state corruption is suspected: rdctl tenant restore --id <TENANT_ID> --from s3://redwood-backups/exports/<TENANT_ID>/prequiesce-<ts>.tar.gz
  c) Re-enable maintenance-mode and notify stakeholders.

Customer communication templates (copy/paste):
- Initial notice (T-72h):
  Subject: Scheduled maintenance for <TENANT_NAME> on <DATE>
  Body: "We plan maintenance for your tenant on <DATE> from <START> to <END> UTC. During the window the tenant will be in maintenance mode and write requests may be rejected. We will provide a post-maintenance report within 24 hours. Contact: <CS_LEAD_EMAIL>."

- At start (T+0):
  Subject: Maintenance started for <TENANT_NAME>
  Body: "Maintenance has started. We are draining active sessions and will perform the agreed tasks. We will update at completion and provide an incident ticket if any rollback occurs."

- Completion (T+2h):
  Subject: Maintenance complete for <TENANT_NAME> (prelim report)
  Body: "Maintenance completed successfully. Initial checks show no impact to production traffic beyond the planned drain. A full metrics summary will be provided in 24 hours."

Observed metrics & dashboards (table):
- Metric | Baseline | Alert threshold | Observation window
- p50 latency | <string: baseline p50> | baseline + 40% | 5m
- p95 latency | <string: baseline p95> | baseline + 40% | 5m
- 5xx error rate | <string: baseline 5xx> | baseline + 2% absolute | 5m
- Active long-poll connections | <count> | > baseline + 50% | 1m

Post-maintenance checklist (T+24h):
1) Deliver full metrics report to customer (compare to baseline with delta).
2) Run service and end-to-end tests; attach results to ticket.
3) Confirm all background jobs completed and no backlog > SLA.
4) Create M&O ticket for any follow-up engineering work.
5) Run retrospective if any rollback or unexpected degradation occurred.

Playbook automation snippets and integrations:
- Example automation step (GitHub Actions) to toggle maintenance mode via API:
  - name: Toggle tenant maintenance
    run: |
      curl -X POST "https://platform-api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/<TENANT_ID>/maintenance" 
        -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.PLATFORM_TOKEN }}" 
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
        -d '{"maintenance": true, "reason":"scheduled-quiesce-{{DATE}}"}'

- Example Datadog monitor expressions to create pre-built monitors:
  - Monitor: tenants.p95_latency{tenant_id:<TENANT_ID>} > baseline_p95 * 1.4 for 3 minutes
  - Monitor: service.5xx_rate{tenant_id:<TENANT_ID>} > baseline_5xx + 0.02 for 5 minutes

Escalation path during maintenance:
1) If a degradation is detected during an observation window, page SRE Ops Lead (PagerDuty) and CS Owner.
2) If rollback is required, declare maintenance rollback in the ticket and notify the customer within 15 minutes.
3) For data loss or corruption suspected, involve Security and Compliance immediately and open a post-incident review.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Background job spike post-failback: mitigate by staggering job resumption and run in controlled batches.
- KV cache desync: restore from pre-quiesce snapshot and run reindex in low-traffic window.
- Model artifact mismatch: keep immutable artifact registry and re-pull verified artifact tag.

Metrics to include in the post-mortem:
- Total maintenance duration (quiesce -> failback complete).
- Number of customer requests rejected with MAINTENANCE code.
- Delta in p95 latency and 5xx compared to baseline (1h, 6h, 24h).
- Any rollback steps executed and time to resolution.

Appendices:
A) Preflight checklist (copyable):
- customer_consent: yes/no
- backup_path: s3://...
- snapshot_checksum: sha256
- cs_owner: name/email
- sre_owner: name/pagerduty

B) Slack templates:
- Start message: "[MAINT] Starting scheduled quiesce for <TENANT_NAME> (ticket #<ID>) — CS: <CS_LEAD> | SRE: <SRE_LEAD>"
- Completion message: "[MAINT] Completed scheduled maintenance for <TENANT_NAME> — prelim checks green. See <ticket> for details."

C) Recovery CLI quick commands:
- Check active requests: rdctl metrics tenants.active_requests --tenant <TENANT_ID>
- Toggle maintenance: rdctl tenant update --id <TENANT_ID> --maintenance <true|false>
- Restore snapshot: rdctl tenant restore --id <TENANT_ID> --from <S3_PATH>

End of playbook.
